useCases.title: GDPR Consent Withdrawal Processing Enforcement
useCases.value: Article 7(3) requires that withdrawal of consent be as easy as giving consent, and processing based on consent must stop after withdrawal. While UC-22.1.5 tracks the consent audit trail, this use cas…

useCases.title: GDPR Consent Mechanism Audit (Lawful Basis Alignment)
useCases.value: By design, consent collection must be granular and verifiable. This use case monitors CMP and web telemetry for consent banner versions, non-essential cookies fired before consent, and mismatches bet…

useCases.title: SOC 2 P1.1 — Privacy notice: consent-record freshness for privacy-notice version changes
useCases.value: Prevents P1.1 findings: 'consent records reference a superseded notice'. Satisfies the '<v-current>' regulator question asked at every annual audit.

useCases.title: Audit-log continuity: detect indexing gap indicating lost evidence
useCases.value: Without continuous audit logs, compliance claims are unfalsifiable. Auditors across GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOC 2, and SOX all treat log-gaps as a finding. This UC lets a customer show the auditor a gr…

useCases.title: Log tamper detection via write-once-read-many chain-of-custody
useCases.value: Produces defensible chain-of-custody evidence: auditors can be shown a 30-day view in which every bucket was either green or had a timestamped remediation ticket.

useCases.title: Indexer replication lag exposing evidence to single-point failure
useCases.value: Turns an otherwise-silent SLO breach into evidence that the control was monitored continuously, even across shards that never had an incident.

useCases.title: Log signing chain integrity — cryptographic signature drift on evidence archive
useCases.value: Replaces the quarterly 'we sampled 10 logs and checked hashes' audit procedure with a continuous control whose output is either 'zero breaks for the period' or a named remediation record. This is the…

useCases.title: DSAR fulfillment SLA tracker with verification evidence trail
useCases.value: Replaces the common 'DPO exports a CSV from OneTrust' evidence pattern with a continuously-measured, tamper-evident record that directly supports auditor questions about Art.12/Art.15 response timeli…

useCases.title: Right-to-erasure propagation completeness across downstream systems
useCases.value: Moves the erasure claim from 'we believe it propagated' to 'we proved it propagated, system by system' — exactly the evidence supervisory authorities ask for on first inspection.

useCases.title: Portability export integrity — signed manifest verification
useCases.value: Adds cryptographic evidence to what is otherwise a 'we generated the file' audit trail.

useCases.title: DSAR identity-verification friction — failed-verification anomaly
useCases.value: Takes the single most common enforcement narrative ('the verification process itself denied the right') and turns it into a measurable metric.

useCases.title: Consent capture evidence freshness — stale-consent alerting
useCases.value: Prevents the 'set-and-forget' consent anti-pattern that surfaces in nearly every GDPR supervisory-authority enforcement action.

useCases.title: Consent withdrawal propagation SLA — downstream stop-processing evidence
useCases.value: Withdrawals that do not propagate are a primary source of supervisory-authority enforcement; this UC turns a weak process control into a tested technical control.

useCases.title: Purpose-limitation enforcement — processing not matching declared purpose
useCases.value: Converts an otherwise-abstract regulatory principle into a continuously-measurable control with evidentiary value.

useCases.title: IAB TCF consent string mutation without user interaction
useCases.value: Catches a pattern that has surfaced repeatedly in EDPB enforcement decisions (Meta, Google ad-tech) before it becomes a supervisory finding.

useCases.title: Cross-border personal-data flow anomaly — egress to unsanctioned jurisdictions
useCases.value: Operationalises a control that is otherwise verifiable only via quarterly desk review of the transfer register.

useCases.title: SCC / adequacy decision reference freshness — stale-safeguard detector
useCases.value: Prevents silent expiration of the legal basis for international transfers — the single most common finding in SCC-era enforcement.

useCases.title: Data localization enforcement — regulated-data must-stay-in-region
useCases.value: Replaces 'we think the bucket is in eu-west-1' with 'we proved every access was in-region for the full audit period'.

useCases.title: Transfer Impact Assessment currency — stale Schrems II assessments
useCases.value: Converts a calendar reminder into a demonstrable control with evidence per-transfer.

useCases.title: Bulk regulated-data export targeting non-adequate jurisdiction
useCases.value: Turns post-hoc 'where did our customer dataset go?' incident forensics into real-time prevention.

useCases.title: Multi-regulator breach-notification SLA tracker (24h NIS2 / 72h GDPR / 72h HIPAA)
useCases.value: Most enforcement actions against supervisory breaches (ICO, DPC, BaFin) focus on notification timeliness. This UC turns the obligation into a visible KPI instead of a post-facto audit finding.

useCases.title: Regulator-portal submission evidence — one-way API acknowledgement audit
useCases.value: Addresses the repeatedly-cited 'we submitted but the authority never acknowledged' defence that now carries no weight in supervisory decisions.

useCases.title: Data-subject breach communication timeline tracker (Art.34 / §164.404)
useCases.value: Data-subject communication is routinely cited in enforcement decisions (Meta, Uber, British Airways); measuring it is the only credible evidence of 'taken reasonable efforts'.

useCases.title: Cross-regulator consistency — divergent material facts across submissions
useCases.value: Prevents the 'regulator cross-reference' problem that has escalated several prominent supervisory cases from technical fines to broader corporate sanction.

useCases.title: Encryption-at-rest coverage gap — unencrypted storage with regulated data
useCases.value: Unencrypted regulated data is the most common PCI 3.5 / HIPAA finding — preventing it from appearing on the audit spreadsheet is the goal.

useCases.title: Subprocessor inventory change — notification SLA to data controllers
useCases.value: Notifications to controllers are a standard audit focus; this UC removes the manual book-keeping.

useCases.title: Developer data-handling training — prod-access engineers lacking training
useCases.value: Links IdP posture to training posture — the evidence auditors actually ask for.

useCases.title: Retention execution evidence — records past retention still present
useCases.value: Retention failures quickly become GDPR enforcement actions — continuous monitoring is the only real defence.

useCases.title: Disposal workflow completion — failed disposals requiring manual review
useCases.value: Ensures the disposal pipeline is as observable as the ingest pipeline.

useCases.title: Retention policy drift — system config vs policy catalogue
useCases.value: Turns retention policy adherence into a continuously-measured metric per system.

useCases.title: Cryptographic erasure attestation — per-asset destruction evidence
useCases.value: Solves the 'how do I prove we actually erased that data?' question that every DPO faces.
